messages:
elaine (sales): Hey team — supporting a new enterprise offline POC. Customer is fully airlocked (no outbound). They want: 1) packaging/installation approach, 2) upgrade cadence and how deltas work offline, 3) offline license activation flow, 4) pricing for reserved capacity on private installs. Any immediate blockers?

sam (solutions): We can ship a self-contained bundle (tar + installer) with all runtime deps. Installer runs entirely offline. For initial activation we create an activation blob that they upload via their bastion.

oscar (eng): Couple of constraints: drivers/CUDA must match our prebuilt runtime. If their nodes are stuck on older drivers we can still run via a container shim but lose some perf optimizations. Also we need to know kernel version for our nvlink hooks.

nina (sec): For verification we require customers to run our checksum script: `sha256sum -c bundle.sha256` and then run the attestation tool. For licensing we support an offline signed license token (we sign a JSON blob with expiry + entitlements). They present it to installer, installer verifies signature.

kyle (cs): Typical POC flow: packaging + internal test (us) 3 business days, customer install + test 1 week, iterate. For upgrades: we offer either a full bundle (quarterly recommended) or monthly security-only patch rollups.

elaine (sales): How do delta patches get applied if they're airgapped? They asked whether we can do incremental diffs or they need full bundles each time.

sam (solutions): We can produce signed delta artifacts (binary diffs + manifest). Customer pulls those into airgapped environment via secure transfer. Installer applies deltas in order. Only caveat: deltas assume you started from a matching base bundle — if mismatch, fallback to full bundle.

oscar (eng): I'll add a preflight check that validates base bundle checksum and runtime compatibility. Example command we give customers: 

```
# run on node before install
curl -sS --output preflight.sh https://internal.redwood.example/preflight.sh  # we hand them the script via secure transfer
bash preflight.sh --verify-bundle /media/bundle.tar.gz
```

and bundle.sha256 looks like: 
```
3b7f9d9e2a4f1e6c3d9b2b8a7f6c5d4e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1  bundle.tar.gz
```

nina (sec): For KMS: we support PKCS#11 import for customer-managed HSMs. For truly airgapped installs they can provide a key import file; we never ship private keys. Also need the security questionnaire completed (network diagrams, certs, APT/YUM restrictions).

legal-bot: Legal note — export control and FIPS requirements may affect delivery. Please attach completed export questionnaire and SCA. We will need a signed MSA addendum for offline distribution.

kyle (cs): For pricing: private/reserved capacity pricing applies when they commit GPU hours or nodes. For POC we typically do a time-limited eval license + a flat support fee for on-site/airgap assistance. If they convert to committed Dedicated pricing we credit the POC fees.

elaine (sales): Good. Customer also asked about upgrade cadence SLA and whether we push security patches automatically. We can't reach into their network, right?

oscar (eng): Correct — we do not push. We provide signed artifacts and a recommended window. If they want us to manage updates we can offer a managed-support add-on where they open a temporary egress tunnel or we run an engineer-assisted update via their bastion.

sam (solutions): Action items: 1) Package template and preflight script (oscar + sam) 2) Offline license token flow doc (nina + legal) 3) POC pricing sheet + eval license terms (kyle + elaine) — aim for draft EOD Friday.

deploy-bot: Created INF-4123: "offline POC packaging + license blob" assigned to oscar, sam — due 2026-04-10.

elaine (sales): I'll collect their OS matrix, firewall rules, and export questionnaire, then loop back. Thanks everyone :pray:
